items.title: Bill Easley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 1, 2021
items.q: "in your interview with Billy Mitchell you talk about this thing and Billy Mitchell used the phrase to you he said, 'Music is a calling.'"

ctx.x: So at the age of 19 or 20 there is a term that my classmates used to use when we were in college and it was sort of we want to make it. We want to make it in the music business.

Good, good, good, good, good idea. My thing, my idea of making it, and to this day, from the time I was — I had specific numbers and everything in my head from the time I understood what was going on. But then and now is to be a working musician. And I know that sounds like an oxymoron but no, that’s pretty much what my goal was and still is, to be playing music and to work and to make this your livelihood. I’ve been able to do that for sixty-some years and don’t try this at home or don’t try this without one…

Well in order to make a living then, I observe in reading about you that a couple of things happened. First of all you learned to play a lot of woodwinds. And second of all you must have had a wide range of music that you decided well I can play with Illinois Jacquet and I can also play with Isaac Hayes. © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-
